key_insight: An AI-driven multi-objective workflow rapidly identified PLGA in situ forming depot formulations that balance drug loading, sustained release, viscosity, and injectability.
engineering_relevance: The study shows how polymer library screening plus AI optimization can compress formulation development timelines and help select candidate long-acting injectables for further in vivo testing.
method: 181 formulations were generated and tested over ~15 weeks.
Drug loading was varied from 6–12% w/w across a broad polymer molecular-weight space.
ANDROMEDA 1 guided broad design-space mapping and targeted multi-objective optimization to find lead candidates.
evidence_signal: Across 181 characterized formulations, four lead candidates at 6%, 9%, and 12% w/w met viscosity and injectability criteria while delivering distinct 30-day in vitro release profiles.
watch_item: The results are based on in vitro screening, so the identified candidates still need in vivo validation and confirmation of manufacturability at scale.
paper_title: Accelerating the Development of PLGA In Situ Forming Depots Through AI-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization
